title: Reconcile the accepted marker-directory rule with the canonical file invariant
decision_statement: The current corpus is contradictory: accepted RFC-038 and repository tooling treat .srs as an implementation-private directory, while canonical Invariant 45 still requires a marker file and the gallery carries that file form; the canonical fold and corpus repair remain unresolved.

sources.excerpt: Current canonical Invariant 45 says a conforming repository must have a .srs marker file.
Accepted RFC-038 rules R3 and R5 use .srs as a skipped implementation-private directory at the repository root.
The current gallery repository artifact is a regular file at .srs rather than a directory.
Issue 313 remains open to reconcile the invariant, projection, gallery artifact, and reference implementation around one marker kind.

alternatives: Fold the accepted directory rule into the canonical invariant and migrate the gallery.
Amend RFC-038 and tooling back to a marker file.
accepted_cost: No final cost is yet effective across all authorities; every option requires amending at least one accepted or canonical source and adding a negative check.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Choosing the convenient live form without reconciling canonical meaning leaves two incompatible repository boundaries.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Any resolution must preserve a clear, discoverable repository boundary and keep private marker content non-authoritative unless explicitly changed.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The conflict is treated as cosmetic even though discovery and validation depend on it.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The directory choice preserves current tooling and the canonical spec repository but changes the canonical invariant and gallery; the file choice reverses those costs.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The fold must name every authority and artifact whose behavior changes.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A local compatibility fix silently creates a third accepted form.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Leaving both forms implicit lets repositories and implementations disagree about whether the same tree is an SRS repository.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Implementation-private state must retain a bounded home after a common marker contract is selected.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Tool-private needs override the shared repository boundary without a normative decision.

coding_notes: D14 preserves the accepted RFC decision as historical evidence; this card separately preserves the unresolved current-authority contradiction and is excluded from bias counts.

title: Make the source-document sidecar authoritative even when content is absent
decision_statement: Source-document identity is discovered from its .meta.json sidecar under sourceDocumentsPath, the documentId comes from that sidecar, and a valid sidecar remains a source-document tombstone when its opaque content payload is absent; sourceDocumentIndex is retired.

sources.excerpt: Accepted Change G retires sourceDocumentIndex, assigns identity to the sidecar, preserves absent-content tombstones, and explicitly supersedes the contrary invariant wording.
Rule R15 makes a parseable sidecar authoritative and permits absent content.
The current canonical invariant still requires sidecar contentPath to resolve, so the accepted supersession is not yet effective in canonical records pending cutover.

alternatives: Require every sidecar to have content.
Drop tombstones when retiring the index.
accepted_cost: Invariant 52 and source-document discovery prose must be rewritten, and a sidecar becomes meaningful membership even without a payload.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Dropping tombstones or treating content presence as identity would erase reference-only source-document meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Opaque payloads remain unparsed and unmanaged payloads remain application-owned.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Sidecars accumulate stale identities whose missing payloads are no longer intentional.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining the index for one legacy role would preserve a shared competing authority.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The existing tombstone capability and documentId identities survive in the sidecar representation.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: The authority flip adopts unindexed sidecars as members without explicit corpus disposition.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Index and sidecar discovery could continue giving different answers about source-document membership.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Payload bytes and unclaimed source material remain outside semantic classification.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One identity rule starts governing application-owned source payload content.

coding_notes: This is independently reversible from generic object discovery. The accepted decision is not yet implemented: current canonical Invariant 52 remains the losing rule until #297 folds the contract.

title: Permit only a reference-preserving scoped cascade on delete
decision_statement: A routine delete normally writes only its target, but deletion of an instance, container, or source document must include only the incident relation or reference targets necessary to avoid an exact-one-resolution violation in the same scoped cascade.

sources.excerpt: Change F resolves the deadlock between isolated writes and fatal dangling references with a narrowly declared cascade, while rejecting a shared tombstone list.
Rule R22 permits and requires only the incident-target cascade needed to preserve R13, forbidding unrelated additions.

alternatives: Leave incident references dangling after deletion.
Maintain a shared tombstone membership list.
accepted_cost: Delete is not always a one-file operation, and importing an older archive can visibly resurrect an object because no instance tombstone list is retained.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Strict one-file isolation would leave a repository fatally inconsistent immediately after a valid delete.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The cascade is limited to named incident targets and must not absorb unrelated cleanup.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Referential closure triggers surprising large deletions without a visible plan or preview.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: A tombstone registry would recreate the shared mutable membership structure RFC-038 removes.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Archive resurrection is visible rather than silently discarded, and root-container deletions remain explicit membership operations.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Rejecting tombstones makes intentional historical deletion impossible to preserve across import.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Purely local delete autonomy would violate the repository-wide reference contract.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Only semantically incident objects join the operation; unrelated objects retain write autonomy.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared-consistency claims justify cascades beyond the smallest closed semantic set.

coding_notes: The cascade is an independently reversible transaction-boundary decision, not merely a mechanical effect of exact-one validation.

title: Define one deterministic logical-identifier order across backends
decision_statement: Every authoritative set enumerates in a deterministic total order by its schema-defined logical identifier using canonical byte-wise UUID comparison, with extensions ordered by kind then ID; filesystem or backend iteration order is never observable enumeration order.

sources.excerpt: Change E explains that platform and backend directory order is unstable and all consumers need one total order.
Rule R14 fixes identifier ordering and forbids exposing storage iteration order.

alternatives: Expose filesystem or map iteration order.
Let each backend choose its native UUID ordering.
accepted_cost: Native database UUID ordering may need normalization, and every adapter must materialize the same canonical comparison rather than expose its cheapest iteration.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Semantically identical repositories would render, export, and diff in unstable orders across runs or backends.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Ordering uses the schema-defined logical identifier and does not change entity identity or meaning.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Presentation stability is mistaken for semantic ordering or used to imply precedence.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Backend migration or platform changes would reorder otherwise identical repository outputs.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Extension sets retain an extensible two-key order rather than a frozen filesystem layout.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Historical byte order prevents a better explicit semantic order when one is later defined.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each adapter or consumer could create different projections from the same logical content.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Storage engines remain free to use any internal ordering and normalize only at the catalog boundary.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The shared ordering contract leaks into storage indexes and constrains local query execution.

coding_notes: This is independently reversible: cross-backend ordering could differ while the logical catalog shape remained unchanged.
